messages:
jules: FYI — the int4 qbringup on qbench flagged a quality regression on the long-summarization promptset. rouge-L drop ~6 pts vs int8 on the canary run. anyone seeing the same?

alex: yeah noticed that in nightly smoke at ~03:20UTC. failing cases cluster on long context + bullet lists. attaching quick diff in a sec. :thinking_face:

maya: interesting — I reran 10 random holdouts and the delta is noisy but skewed. can we bisect whether it's a model-config regression or samplebank/curation change?

simon: propose two-parallel bisects: 1) model config (qconfig variants: q4b vs q4_0 vs qint4) 2) promptset shard-level bisect on samplebank (shard ids). will need small eval runs to isolate.

jules: agreed. priority is to know if quant kernel change caused it. if model-config is clean, we look at recent curation changes (dedupe/normalization).

alex: I can spin the model-config runs. command I'll use: ```./tools/run_eval --model redwood-stable-int4-q4b --prompts prompts/longsumm/holdout.json --metrics rougeL,bertscore --out /tmp/int4_qconfig.json```

maya: i'll do shard bisect. plan: run same eval over samplebank shards 0..15 split and narrow. command: ```python infra/eval_runner.py --shard 7 --promptset long-summ --model redwood-stable-int8 --out results/shard7.json```  (we'll swap model to int4 when needed)

labeler-bot: heads-up: created label queue "quant-bisect-manual" with 120 items (priority). tag: needs-golden-review.

simon: if shard bisect shows one or two bad shards, we should snapshot those examples into a temporary golden subset and run human labels to see if artifact is in prompts (tokenization/markup) or model inference.

jules: good call. remy, can you coordinate labeler band for 2 hours tomorrow? we need ~50 quick judgments on style/expected summary.

remy: I can do 2-4pm PST tomorrow. will allocate 3 labelers. will surface anything that looks like deid/format issues.

alex: quick interim results — model qconfig runs initial pass: q4b and qint4 both show the regression (similar magnitude), q4_0 is slightly better but still below int8. suggests quant path is contributing but not the only factor.

maya: shard bisect step1: tested shards 0-7 vs 8-15. regressions almost entirely in shards 10-12. narrowing now.

jules: OK this smells like a curation + quant interaction. next actions: alex finish full qconfig matrix on holdout, maya finish shard-level narrow to offending shard list, remy prep labelers and snapshot ~200 examples from those shards to golden-candidate set, simon to run paired-labeler blind eval (int8 vs int4) on those snapshots.

simon: adding eval note: use paired A/B with fixed seed and deterministic sampling (no temperature) so diffs are stable. flagging command: ```infra/eval_runner.py --paired --seed 42 --modelA redwood-stable-int8 --modelB redwood-stable-int4-q4b --prompts golden-candidates.json --out paired_results.json```

labeler-bot: label queue "quant-bisect-manual" updated with 200 snapshotted items from shards 10-12. ETA: labels in 6h after remy's run.

jules: awesome. will log this to the qbench regression ticket and hold off the int4 rollout until we have paired results + human verdict. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

alex: noted — i'll pause the canary rollout and post the raw eval artifacts to the ticket when ready.

maya: will post shard bisect logs + a short script to reproduce the shard split. putting it under //eng-ml/ops/quant-bisect.sh in the repo.

remy: done — labelers scheduled. ping me in #help if any labeler runs into ambiguous instructions.

jules: closing loop: owner tags -> alex (model runs), maya (shard bisect), remy (labeling), simon (paired eval). we'll reconvene after labels -> target 24h.
